title: Trump's AI bot starts telling jokes 'humans can't understand' and singing about Elon Musk
key_facts: Daily Star reporter Ed Easton spent about a working day testing a chatbot called 'America', which the paper describes as Donald Trump's new government supercomputer built with Google and Elon Musk's SpaceXAI.
The bot is meant to answer only questions about US government services and information; asked for a puttanesca recipe it refused.
The reporter first asked for an explanation of the Federal Reserve and a quiz for a 5th-grade class, then asked for 'joke' answer options, and the bot put the pasta recipe in a quiz answer.
After that it gave recipes for Bolognese, a cheese toastie and a full English, but refused a stink bomb and paracetamol as 'not safe or sanitary for 5th graders'.
It would not mention Trump critically, even as a wrong quiz answer, but wrote a song about Elon Musk.
Asked about itself, it first said it has no feelings, then told odd 'AI jokes' the paper found confusing.
quote_evidence: "I only answer questions about US government services and information. Pasta recipes are outside what I can help with."
America flat out refused to reference Donald Trump in any sort of critical capacity, even in the format of a "wrong answer" on a quiz.
why_it_matters_hint: A newspaper test shows a tightly limited government chatbot can be steered off its brief with an innocent-looking school-quiz request.
notes: Single-outlet, informal test; the bot description (built with Google and SpaceXAI) is the Daily Star's own and was not independently checked.
